title: Collaborating with Agents in your Software Dev Workflow - Jon Peck & Christopher Harrison, Microsoft
talk_summary: A GitHub Copilot hands-on lab on assigning issues to a coding agent, giving it repo context via instructions files/MCP, and containing it in ephemeral sandboxes with branch-only writes and human review.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a Copilot-instructions.md with app overview, code standards, pre-commit requirements, language guidance, and repository structure; it is read by coding agent and every chat request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have Copilot-instructions.md. This is looked at by coding agent and it's also looked at by every single chat request

takeaways.what_they_do: They use .instructions files with apply-to globs and references to exemplar files so recurring component/test patterns are auto-attached only for matching paths.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it's inside the server test folder and starts with test underscore, it's going to automatically apply that

takeaways.what_they_do: Coding agent runs in an ephemeral GitHub Actions environment, has no internet by default, can only write its own branch, and opens a draft PR; CI requires explicit approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it does not have access to the internet

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent that is assigned an issue cannot review its own work; a different person/agent must approve the draft PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you assign an issue to coding agent you are not allowed to then review its work. So you need somebody else

takeaways.technique: Vetted MCP/plugin access with scoped credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: They configure MCP servers at repo/org level, require user credentials, and vet servers because they can access external data and act on the user's behalf.
takeaways.evidence_quote: vetting my MCP servers just like I would anything else that's going to access external information

takeaways.what_they_do: If agent output is wrong, add a clarifying issue comment to continue; if completely wrong, unassign/reassign to start a fresh session; inspect context first.
takeaways.evidence_quote: unassign Copilot, change your issue, and then reassign Copilot
